chunks: From Zurarah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was sitting with him,

concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it… and whoever brings an evil deed, he shall not be recompensed except like it, and they will not be wronged.' Does it apply to these, from among those who do not recognize this affair (of Wilayah)?
He replied: It is exclusively for the believers.
ai.seo_question: Does the Quranic promise of tenfold reward apply to all people or only to true believers?
ai.summary: Zurarah narrates that Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarified the scope of Surah Al-An'am 6:160, specifying that the tenfold reward for good deeds and exact retribution for evil are exclusively reserved for those who possess true faith (Iman) and recognize the Wilayah of the Imams. This distinction highlights the Shia theological principle that mere outward action is insufficient without the underlying spiritual recognition of divine authority, thereby elevating the status of the 'Mu'minun' above general believers.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 51. Zurarah narrated: I was seated in the presence of Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) when he was asked
concerning the words of Allah [M.G]: Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it… [Holy Quran 6/160], 'Does it apply to those whom do not confess of this affair (of Wilayah)?’
'It is exclusively for believers,' he replied.
